title: Idempotent Payment Gateway
tagline: A charge API that survives client retries, flaky processors, and duplicate webhooks without ever charging twice.
summary: You build the core of a card-payment gateway: an idempotency store that detects replays and conflicts by fingerprint, a payment state machine with partial refunds and versioned history, a retrying processor client with full-jitter backoff, a retry budget and a circuit breaker, and a signed webhook dispatcher with at-least-once delivery and consumer-side dedupe. Everything runs on an injected clock and a seeded random source, so every schedule and every signature is reproducible.
youWillBuild: An in-memory payment gateway where the same request can be sent any number of times and money moves exactly once.

languageWhy.Java: Records, sealed-style enums and EnumMap give the state machine and the transition table a compact, type-checked shape; javax.crypto.Mac and MessageDigest.isEqual are the production HMAC tools.
languageWhy.Python: hashlib, hmac.compare_digest and frozen dataclasses are the production-grade pieces in the standard library; the xorshift64* Rng is ported bit-for-bit, so a retry schedule drawn in Python is the one the Java tests expect.
languageWhy.Go: Constructors return (value, error) and misuse of the store or the state machine is a sentinel error you test with errors.Is, so 'illegal state' is a value, not a stack trace; a sync.Mutex inside the store is the explicit form of Java's synchronized, and crypto/hmac plus hmac.Equal are the standard-library pieces a real webhook receiver uses.

skills: Scope idempotency keys per account, fingerprint the request body with SHA-256, and classify every call as NEW, REPLAY, CONFLICT or IN_PROGRESS with a TTL
Drive a payment through an explicit transition table with versioned history and partial refunds in integer minor units
Retry only retryable failures with exponential backoff, full jitter from a seeded source, a retry budget and a CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN circuit breaker
Sign webhook events with HMAC-SHA256 and a timestamp, verify them inside a tolerance window, deliver at-least-once with dead-lettering, and dedupe on the consumer

prerequisites.title: Idempotency Keys: Exactly-Once Effects on At-Least-Once Networks

stages.title: Idempotency Store
stages.summary: A store keyed by (merchant, idempotency key) that fingerprints the canonical request with SHA-256 and answers NEW, REPLAY, CONFLICT or IN_PROGRESS, with records that expire on an injected clock.

stages.title: Payment State Machine
stages.summary: A Payment that moves created -> processing -> succeeded | failed (or canceled) through one transition table, keeps a versioned transition log, and refunds in parts until it is fully refunded.

stages.title: Retries, Backoff and a Circuit Breaker
stages.summary: A processor client that retries only UNAVAILABLE with capped exponential backoff and full jitter from a seeded source, stops when a retry budget drains, and sits behind a CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN breaker; then the Gateway that ties the store, the state machine and the client together.

stages.title: Signed Webhooks, At-Least-Once
stages.summary: Lifecycle events signed with HMAC-SHA256 over a timestamp and the body, verified inside a tolerance window with a constant-time compare, delivered at-least-once on a retry schedule with a dead-letter list, and deduped by event id on the consumer.
